chunks: And Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Jawza' al-Munbih ibn Abdullah, from al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him):

Regarding the prayer over a child, he used to say: 'O God, make him a precursor and merit and reward for his parents and for us.' Then the Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'Even if he is weak (a young child).'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ عَلَى الطِّفْلِ: Prayer over a child (funeral prayer for a child)
key_terms.سَلَفًا: A precursor or forerunner (in good deeds)
key_terms.فَرَطًا: A precursor or one who goes before (leading the way)
key_terms.مُسْتَضْعَفًا: Weak or frail (referring to a young child)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited for a child during the funeral prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali (AS) provides the specific supplication for the funeral prayer of a child, emphasizing their role as a 'precursor' (farat) and 'reward' (ajr) for parents and the community. Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that this practice applies even to infants or those who were weak, highlighting the continuity of spiritual merit regardless of the child's age or duration of life. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the intergenerational spiritual connection and the accumulation of good deeds through familial bonds.
